office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, ferries, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Eight-year Democratic incumbent Debra Lekanoff faces Republican Cindy Carter of Orcas Island, whose campaign centers on repealing the 2026 tax on income over $1 million that Lekanoff voted for. Carter also campaigns on spending accountability and cutting the carbon tax; neither candidate has stated a position on the 2026 initiatives.

candidates.summary: Eight-year State Representative and vice chair of the House Health Care and Wellness Committee, campaigning on affordability, ferries, salmon and the Salish Sea, unions and reproductive freedom.
highlights: Voted for the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and the 2025 B&O and services tax bills [S3][S5][S6]
Co-sponsored and voted for the 2025 limit on residential rent and fee increases [S7]
Voted for ESHB 1296, the 2025 changes to the parental-rights law that I-1 would undo [S4]
Says she helped fund three new ferries and accelerated ferry hiring [S1]

taxes.basis: Voted yes on ESSB 6346 and on the 2025 B&O (EHB 2081) and services excise (ESSB 5814) tax bills.

housing.basis: Co-sponsored and voted for the EHB 1217 rent-increase limit and backs low-income housing investment, alongside support for middle housing and zoning plans.

climate.basis: Pledges to protect salmon, forests and the Salish Sea; 2024 website calls for green-building standards, retrofit and renewable incentives and climate planning.

social.basis: Pledges to defend reproductive freedom and the right to choose; no stated position on LGBTQ+ policy or school sports.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296 on House passage and final passage; no statement on notification or opt-outs.

experience.basis: Eight years in the House, committee vice chair, facing a challenger with no elected office.

candidates.summary: Orcas Island former hospital laboratory technologist and Republican Party officer campaigning as "No Income Tax Carter" to repeal the 2026 income tax and restrain state spending.
highlights: Central pledge is to repeal the 2026 tax on income over $1 million [S1][S4]
Says the state has a spending problem and cites unaudited child-care spending [S3]
Would eliminate the carbon tax to lower gas and food prices [S3]
Opposes a universal health-care system and favors catastrophic plans and interstate insurance competition [S3]

taxes.basis: Pledges to repeal the income tax, says there is no need to increase any taxes and would cut existing ones.

spending.basis: Says Washington has a spending problem, cites audit findings and lists eliminating fraud and ineffective programs as priorities.

climate.basis: Would eliminate the 'Carbon Emissions Tax' to lower gasoline and food prices.

healthcare.basis: Argues against a universal health-care system; favors catastrophic insurance, interstate competition and private practice.

safety.basis: Says the best way to improve safety is to get criminals off the streets through joint enforcement, while also listing drug treatment.

immigration.basis: Favors 'coming into compliance with federal law' and working with federal authorities; does not name immigration enforcement directly.

local-control.basis: Calls one-size-fits-all state water rules damaging to the district and wants to roll back state regulation.

experience.basis: No elected office; long service as a county and state Republican Party officer.
